tory_boatman.text: Back to the mainland? The sea's in a fair mood. For now.

then.text: Fáilte go Toraigh! Welcome to Tory! Oh, it's yourself. The king's own friend. Mind the steps, they're slippy with seaweed and royal dignity.
You saw the pretender off, and there's a band tuning up in the club. So. They want me, then? Me? I only came down to meet the boat.

The islanders gather at the pier. Somebody produces a chair. Somebody else produces a fiddle. There is no crown, so the youngest child on the island puts a lobster pot on Séamus's head, and everyone agrees it suits him.
Right. As my first act as Rí Thoraí, I declare a céilí. As my second act, I'd like to sit down.
That's a bit of Tory clay. They say no rat can live on the island because of it. Keep it in your bag and see what it keeps away.
Did you ask the gallery? They know everyone on the island; they've painted half of us. Badly, the half they didn't like.

else.text: {greeting} You're the one helping choose the king? Well, God help you. Nobody can agree. The painters want a painter, the fishermen want a fisherman, and everyone wants it not to be them.
Talk to the gallery keeper. If anyone can count the votes on this island, it's the gallery. Nobody leaves without being sold a picture.

then.text: You have him, Balor himself, in your bag. I hope you keep his eye shut. I'd sleep better.
You caught him? Balor of the Evil Eye? The Fomorian king, tamed by a walker with a bag? Well, I'll need a new ending for the story.
Here, take these. Barmbrack, for luck. You'll need it, travelling with that one.

else.text: Do you know the story of Balor? A king of the Fomorians, the old sea giants, with one great eye that killed whatever it looked upon. It took four men to lift the lid.
A prophecy said his own grandson would kill him, so he locked his only daughter in a tower on this island. Well. That went the way those things always go.
The grandson was Lugh, and Lugh put a sling-stone through that eye. They say Balor's still out at the fort on the east cliffs, all the same, sleeping it off.

then.text: Fine. FINE. I didn't want to be king of a rock in the sea anyway. I'll be king of a nice golf club in Wicklow instead.

else.text: A céilí band? For Séamus? Absolutely not. I've had a crown on order from Dublin for a week. I'm the obvious candidate. I have a blazer.

then.text: ...I may have misjudged the island. Go on, crown your fisherman.

else.text: Hello! Hello! I'm standing for king. Vote for me and I'll put in a golf course. And a car park. And a second car park for the first car park.
Some islanders nearby are looking at him the way the sea looks at a sandcastle.

then.text: The wind drops. The sea goes flat and grey as pewter. On the headland, a huge shape you took for a rock stirs, and something like a great eyelid, the size of a door, begins to lift.
Who walks on my fort? I have slept here since the sling-stone. The islanders have a new king, I hear. They always have a king. I was one, once.
Look away, little walker. Whatever I look upon withers. Or look at me, and let us see which of us blinks.
The great eye closes, slowly, like a door being shut against the weather. Balor settles into your snare, and for the first time in a very long while, the east end of Tory is quiet.

else.text: The eyelid comes down. The storm comes up. When it clears, there is only a rock on the headland, and the faint smell of thunder.
A huge grey rock squats on the end of the headland, with a crack across it like a closed eye. The gulls won't land on it.
The islanders are busy choosing a king. Perhaps the rock is waiting for that, too.

then.text: Aon, dó, trí, tarraing! One, two, three, pull! That is all the rowing Irish you need.

else.text: On Tory we row a curach, a thin lath boat, out to the rocks when the wind lets us, which is not often. The island is a Gaeltacht, and its rowers do not waste syllables.
Race of the Waves, is it? Cailín sent you with her Irish and a good word for us? Then Tory will row. Tell Dingle the island is in, and that we will be sick on the way back.
Oh, you are one of those who waits for the ferry. We have all the time in the world, and Tory has none of the Wi-Fi.
